recipes.reason: Restore wet/dry/topping groups and mutually exclusive fruit and milk alternatives lost in flattening.
ingredients: Wet mixture: 200 g very soft margarine
Wet mixture: 400 g white granulated sugar
Wet mixture: 75 g dried grated coconut
Wet mixture: zest of a lemon or grated ginger
Wet mixture: 250 ml cold soy milk
Dry mixture: 2 sachets (40 g) baking powder
Dry mixture: 100 g unsweetened cocoa powder
Add-ins, option 1: 450 ml soy milk and 2 glasses (500 g) cranberries or lingonberries
Add-ins, option 2 instead: 700 ml soy milk and 2 small apples cut into small pieces
steps: Beat the wet mixture ingredients for 10 minutes until creamy, adding its 250 ml soy milk gradually.
Combine the dry mixture ingredients, then sift loosely to aerate and remove lumps.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Add the wet mixture and one chosen add-in option to the dry mixture. Stir briefly until smooth. Do not overmix, since the batter will deflate and become tough.
Spread in a large baking pan lined with baking paper.
Bake for 20 minutes. Turn off the oven and continue cooking in residual heat for 15 minutes. Let cool.
Unmold and remove the baking paper.
Melt chocolate couverture over a double boiler. Spread over the cake and sprinkle with grated coconut while still soft.

ingredients: 2 sticks (½ lb / 225 g / 1 cup) butter, softened
¾ cup (180 ml) granulated white sugar
¾ cup (180 ml) packed brown sugar
2 ¼ cups (600 ml / 290 g) all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon dry ground lemon or orange peel (optional)
2 cups (480 ml / 12 oz) semi-sweet chocolate morsels / chips
5 oz (150 g) chopped nuts, such as groundnuts (optional)
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F (source also gives 210°C), or 350°F (source also gives 195°C) for chewy cookies.
Cream butter, granulated sugar, and brown sugar in a large mixer bowl.
Add eggs one at a time, beating until fully incorporated.
Add vanilla extract and beat in.
In a small bowl sift together dry ingredients except chocolate and nuts. Add to wet mixture in two parts and fold until combined; overbeating can develop gluten and alter texture.
Stir in chocolate chips and nuts if using.
Drop rounded tablespoons onto ungreased baking sheets. Parchment paper or nonstick pans can help if sticking occurs.
Bake for 10–12 minutes or until golden brown. Let stand about 1 minute, then move from hot baking sheet to a wire rack to cool.

ingredients: 1 cup (250 ml / 8.5 fl oz) vegetable oil
2 cups (150 g / 5.3 oz) pecans or almonds, chopped
1 cup (100 g / 3.5 oz) granola, rolled oats or Grape-Nuts
steps: Preheat oven to 375°F.
In a large bowl, combine wet ingredients.
Sift flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, soda, and cloves together in a separate bowl.
Blend dry into wet ingredients.
Mix in nuts, granola, and chocolate chips.
Drop spoonfuls onto a greased cookie sheet.
Bake for 10–12 minutes, then cool.

recipes.reason: Restore biscuit and filling ingredient groups so separate egg whites and sugar portions remain distinct.
ingredients: Marzipan biscuits: 2 ea. (60 g) pasteurized egg whites
Vanilla filling: 250 g white granulated sugar
Vanilla filling: 4 ea. (140 g) pasteurized egg whites
Vanilla filling: concentrated or dry flavoring (optional)
steps: For the biscuits, mix 100 g icing sugar and 2 egg whites in a bowl.
Mix this into marzipan in stages until uniform.
Pipe flat round biscuits about 5 cm across with a pastry bag.
Bake at 190°C until golden, about 10 minutes.
Cool to ambient temperature.
For the filling, mix 250 g sugar, water, and glucose syrup in a saucepan and heat to exactly 117°C.
Meanwhile beat the 4 filling egg whites lightly with 15 g sugar.
Gradually pour hot sugar mixture into these whites while beating.
Whip until very stiff.
Split vanilla bean, scrape out seeds, and mix seeds with 1 teaspoon icing sugar. Stir into the filling with optional flavoring until uniform, without deflating the meringue.
Pipe 5 cm tall meringue tops onto biscuits, ensuring foam adheres.
Leave at room temperature or refrigerate while preparing the coating.
Finely chop chocolate.
Melt half carefully in a bain-marie, aiming for 48–50°C.
Put remaining chocolate in a bowl large enough to submerge a treat. Add ⅔ of melted chocolate and melt together without heating. Add more melted chocolate only if lumps remain. Do not exceed 34°C.
Dip meringue tops into chocolate, covering all meringue and optionally the biscuit.
Sprinkle or roll in desiccated coconut, then set. If chocolate starts setting, use warm melted chocolate rather than reheating.

ingredients: 4 squares (4 oz / 115 g) unsweetened chocolate, melted
steps: Mix oil, chocolate, and granulated sugar.
Blend in one egg at a time until well mixed. Add vanilla.
Stir flour, baking powder, and salt into chocolate mixture.
Chill several hours or overnight.
Heat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Drop teaspoonfuls of dough into confectioners' sugar.
Roll in sugar and shape into balls.
Place about 2 inches (5 cm) apart on a greased baking sheet.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes.

ingredients: 2 ½ cups (550 g / 1.2 lb) white granulated sugar
½ cup (125 g / 4.4 oz) margarine or butter
⅔ cup (160 ml / 5.4 oz) evaporated milk
2 cups (160 g / 5.6 oz) semi-sweet chocolate chips
¾ cup (75 g / 2.6 oz) chopped walnuts
steps: Line a 9-inch square or 13-by-9-inch pan with foil extending over the sides; butter the foil.
In a large saucepan combine sugar, margarine, and evaporated milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
After 5 minutes of constant stirring, remove from heat.
Add marshmallow creme and chocolate chips; blend until smooth. Stir in walnuts and vanilla.
Pour into prepared pan and cool to room temperature.
Score into 36–48 squares. Refrigerate until firm.
Lift foil to remove fudge from pan, peel foil from sides, and cut through scored lines with a large knife. Refrigerate for storage.
